- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish prior — cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising) and sentiment was bullish, reduce forecast slope; if sentiment turns bearish, allow downward drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term momentum; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, use 14-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model tends to lag; delay forecast correction by 1-2 days if sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts — suppress forecast rise if sentiment >0.7 and price < previous 5-day avg.
